title: Strip Out AI and the S&P 500 Looks Very Different, Goldman Index Shows
key_facts: S&P 500 up 18.3% in six months to 7,818.93 at Tuesday's close (6 Oct 2026); record close.
Goldman's ex-AI index (SPXXAI) up 6.7% to 3,123.24, 6.4% below its 52-week high.
Goldman built the index in February to let clients hedge AI exposure, per Axios.
It excludes AI enablers, about 45% of the S&P 500 at launch.
AMD, Marvell, Synopsys and Cadence each gained 20% or more in about 20 trading days, per CNBC.
Schwab's Kevin Gordon: average stock fell 14% peak to trough since early August.
quote_evidence: The S&P 500 has gained 18.3% in six months, against 6.7% for Goldman Sachs' index excluding artificial intelligence (AI) enablers.
The split suggests the benchmark's records now rest on AI-linked stocks.
why_it_matters_hint: Market gains are concentrated in AI-linked stocks.
notes: Original by Darryn Pollock at BeInCrypto; read on Yahoo Finance. Cites Axios and CNBC.
